title: Grand Ronde Reservation Act Amendment of 2023
official_summary:
Grand Ronde Reservation Act Amendment of 2023

This act revises the land claims of the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde Community of Oregon. In particular, the act specifies that only the tribe's claims to the 84 acres of land known as the Thompson Strip, rather than the tribe's claims to any lands within Oregon, are extinguished.

Additionally, the act prohibits gaming on any real property obtained by the tribe as part of a land claim settlement approved by the United States, including any real property purchased with funds granted as part of any land claim settlement.

summary.headline: Law narrows the Grand Ronde Tribes' land claims given up to just the 84-acre Thompson Strip and bans gaming on settlement lands.
summary.what_it_does: This law changes an earlier law about the land claims of the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde Community of Oregon. Before, the tribe's claims to any lands in Oregon were ended. Now, only the tribe's claims to an 84-acre area called the Thompson Strip are ended. The law also bans gaming on any land the tribe gets through a federally approved land claim settlement, including land bought with settlement money.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Confederated Tribes of the Grand Ronde Community of Oregon
who_it_affects.how: Their tribe keeps the ability to pursue land claims in Oregon outside the Thompson Strip, but cannot run gaming on land gained through a land claim settlement.

who_it_affects.group: Other Oregon tribes and landholders near possible claim areas
who_it_affects.how: The Grand Ronde tribe's land claims elsewhere in Oregon are no longer treated as ended, which may affect future land claim matters.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2023; the summary does not list a separate start date.
